title: reading-velocity-inference-notes-nathan-cho-2026-12-08
content:
TL;DR
- Quick pass on 6 papers/blogs about request-level latency vs batching vs cache hit tradeoffs. Trying to map to a 2-week spike experiment we can run on staging.
- Big-picture: small changes to request routing + adaptive KV cache policy look promising for reducing p50 by ~10–25% on mixed workloads while holding throughput. But need to watch tail.

Papers & posts skimmed (notes to self)
1) "Adaptive Microbatching for Low-latency Inference" (conference poster, 2026) — idea: scheduler that slices microbatches based on current queue latency targets and cold-starts. Notes: cheaper than full preemption; assumes accurate short-term latency prediction. Curious how it reacts to bursty chat traffic.
2) Blog: "Prefix KV caching and conditional materialization" (engineering blog, Oct 2026) — stores compacted prefix states keyed by coarse convo-hash, materialize if predicted reuse. Notes: storage vs compute tradeoff; potential to compress with quantized KV.
3) Paper: "Tail-aware routing for heterogeneous GPUs" (SysML 2026) — sends high-SLO requests to low-latency pool, others to cost-optimized pool. Uses a small RL policy. Notes: Redwood already has routing policy hooks; could prototype simple heuristic (SLO tag + recent tail metric) before any RL.
4) Poster: "KV eviction policies for long contexts" — LRU variants perform poorly when contexts have long identical prefixes; frequency-aware eviction better. Could be a win for multi-turn chat.
5) Ops writeup: "Measuring p99 contributions: batching vs worker scheduling" (internal, Q3 2026) — practical logs we generated. Re-read to align metrics.
6) Quick read: "Using model distillation to reduce token compute for repetitive prompts" — compress recurring prompt sequences into short tokens. Experimental but interesting for assistant templates.

Key takeaways
- Target use-case: chat agents with medium-length contexts (2–8k tokens) and a mix of 1–10 concurrent requests per user. Latency-sensitive p50 is crucial for UX; p95/p99 are where we need fallbacks.
- Immediate levers we can try: adaptive microbatching + SLO-aware routing + smarter KV eviction. Those three interact: batching can increase p50 if it delays short queries; routing can isolate short queries to keep p50 low; eviction changes cache hit rate which changes effective batching.
- Metric framing: track request-level p50/p95/p99; per-request token-cost; batch-size distribution; KV-cache hit ratio by prefix-length bucket.

Hypotheses (to test)
H1: SLO-tagged routing to a reserved low-latency pool reduces p50 by ~15% for short queries with <50ms added infra latency and minimal cost increase.
H2: Frequency-biased KV-eviction improves cache hit rate for multi-turn conversational sessions by 8–12% (helps reuse), reducing token compute cost.
H3: Adaptive microbatching with a short-latency fallback (single-request processing if latency target at risk) can keep p95 < target while maintaining batching efficiency ~70% of baseline.

Experiment plan (2-week spike)
Week 1: measurement + canary prototypes
- Day 1-2: instrument metrics we lack: per-request SLO tag, batch wait time histogram, KV hit by prefix length. Add telemetry hooks in staging. (Linked: GH PR above).
- Day 3-4: baseline sweep: run replayed production traces through staging runtime to capture baseline numbers. Save trace segments for regression tests.
- Day 5-7: implement simple SLO-aware router (heuristic: requests with header X-SLO: interactive go to pool A; others to pool B). Canary on small % of traffic in staging.
Week 2: policies + analysis
- Day 8-10: KV-eviction prototype: implement LFU-ish within shard with aging. Run same traces.
- Day 11-12: microbatching: plug in adaptive microbatcher variant B (short sleep cap 4ms, max batch 64). Test with and without routing.
- Day 13-14: analyze results, write quick findings doc + next actions (rollout gating).

Implementation notes / TODOs
- Instrumentation: add tag to trace span for "routing_decision" and "batch_delay_ms". Need tracing hooks in runtime (see INF-1298).
- Experiment config: feature-flag everything; make router a config in runtime.json rather than hardcoded.
- Data retention: store sample traces for 7 days only. Avoid storing user prompt content (masking!).
- Safety: ensure fallback to model-variant chain if cache fails. Add automated canary kill switch.

Open questions / risks
- How do we anticipate background cache warmups affecting our staged traces? Staging traces often have cold caches. We'll need to replay warmed traces too.
- Resource accounting: SLO pool costs — are we okay to burn dedicated small nodes? Finance ok? Pinged @Ava in Slack.
- Interaction with quantization: different quantized kernels might change per-token time unpredictably. Microbatcher predictions will need to be kernel-aware.
- User privacy: logged traces must be hashed & salted; confirm privacy review with security.

Loose notes to self (brain dump)
- Could borrow RL idea later but start with simple thresholds. RL adds complexity and hard-to-debug non-determinism.
- If frequency-aware eviction helps, think about sharded frequency counters per-customer to avoid cross-tenant bias.
- For prefix compression: try tiny seq2seq distillation on frequent templates (customer-specific); maybe an offline step.

Communications / links to share with team
- Draft thread for #serving-runtime: outline experiment + ask for volunteers for code review and canary ops.
- Short slide: 1) problem + metrics 2) experiment plan 3) expected outcome 4) risks. Target ops sync Friday.

Action items (short)
- [ ] Add batch_delay_ms and routing_decision spans (Nathan) — due Day 2
- [ ] Create replay job for warmed traces (Ravi) — due Day 3
- [ ] Prototype SLO-router config (Ava + Nathan) — due Day 5
- [ ] Data privacy check with security (ask @Mia) — due Day 4

Reminders / todos for future reading
- Find more on "conditional KV materialization" (author: Elena Marquez) — paper link somewhere in my inbox.
- Re-check SysML paper for RL details if routing heuristics fail.

End notes
- Keep this doc messy; will refine to a formal spike brief if results look promising.
- If anyone reading: add quick comments inline or ping me in Slack with 'SLO-spike' tag.

-- Nathan
(quick scratchpad; not intended as a final doc)
